options.A: The study's participants were all volunteers who were already predisposed to energy conservation, potentially biasing the outcomes.
options.B: Historical data indicate that the Jevons paradox has been observed consistently in markets for transportation and lighting but not for major household appliances.
options.C: Households that achieve lower utility bills through efficiency upgrades frequently allocate the savings to purchase other goods whose manufacture and use are energy-intensive.
options.D: As energy-efficient appliances become more prevalent, the resulting reduction in aggregate energy demand can drive down energy prices, which in turn incentivizes greater overall energy use.
options.E: The increased affordability of operating energy-efficient appliances leads to a marked rise in the total number of such appliances in households, offsetting the per-unit savings.
